sections.label: Online Criminal Harms Bill scope
sections.summary: The Online Criminal Harms Bill focuses on online content or activity that is criminal or facilitates or abets crimes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Online Criminal Harms Bill we are debating today focuses instead on online content or activity which is criminal in nature, or which is used to facilitate or abet crimes.

sections.label: Directions to online service providers
sections.summary: The Bill allows Directions to be issued to online service providers, other entities, or individuals when specified criminal offences take place.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: First, the Bill allows Directions to be issued to online service providers, other entities, or individuals, when specified criminal offences take place.

sections.label: Lower threshold and scam systems
sections.summary: The threshold to issue Directions should be lower than for other specified criminal offences, and designated online services must counter scams and malicious cyber activities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The threshold to issue Directions should therefore be lower than for the other specified criminal offences.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We will also require designated online services to put in place systems and processes to counter scams and malicious cyber activities.

sections.label: Malware in investment and job scams
sections.summary: Victims may download malware that steals login credentials or personal information, commonly used in investment and job scams.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Victims may also inadvertently download malware that have the ability to steal their login credentials or other personal information.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Such methods are commonly used for investment and job scams, which together saw close to 10,000 cases in 2022, with victims losing more than $300 million.

sections.label: Lower threshold for scam Directions
sections.summary: Clause 6(1)(b) introduces a lower threshold for issuing Directions for scams and malicious cyber activity offences specified under part 2 of the First Schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Faced with such opponents, Members might understand why our response needs to also be "kiasu"; to be extraordinarily careful.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This is why clause 6(1)(b) of the Bill introduces a lower threshold for issuing Directions for scams and malicious cyber activity offences that are specified under part 2 of the First Schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Law enforcement would then be able to issue Directions proactively, once such activities are detected, and even before an offence is committed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For instance, we could issue Access Blocking Directions to Internet service providers to prevent the blank websites I mentioned earlier from being accessed by Singapore users, even before scammers activate these sites.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We would also be able to issue App Removal Directions to remove scam apps that are used to commit scam offences, from Singapore app storefronts and third-party app stores.

sections.label: Rectification Notice for non-compliance
sections.summary: Clause 23 allows the competent authority to serve a Rectification Notice on non-compliant designated online services before escalation to prosecution.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: If designated online services are found to be non-compliant with the codes of practice, clause 23 allows that the competent authority be able to serve the providers of these services with a Rectification Notice to correct the non-compliance by a specified time, before escalation to prosecution.

sections.label: Appeals, codes and information powers
sections.summary: Appeals against designation, codes of practice and Implementation Directives go to the Minister for Home Affairs, and Clause 48 lets officers request information from online service providers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Appeals against designation of online services, the application and content of codes of practice, and Implementation Directives will be heard by the Minister for Home Affairs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, an appeal by a designated online service against a provision in a code of practice may be resolved through varying that provision.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This will, however, impact other designated providers that are similarly subject to that code and thus should be decided by the Minister for Home Affairs.This appeal mechanism is similar to that provided for appeals against codes of practice in other legislation such as the Broadcasting Act, which are also appealed to the relevant Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 48 provides that Police officers and enforcement officers may request information from online service providers or owners of online locations where there is reasonable suspicion that a specified offence has been committed and there is online activity on that online service or location which is in aid of the specified offence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This is to facilitate investigations and criminal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: These powers also apply to entities that are based overseas and information which is stored overseas.

sections.label: WP support for online content rules
sections.summary: The Workers' Party will support rules aimed at online content when they are in Singaporeans' interest, such as with this Bill, but not otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party (WP) will support rules aimed at online content when they are in Singaporeans' interest, such as with this Bill, but not otherwise.

sections.label: WP position on FICA
sections.summary: The WP did not vote in favour of FICA, saying it confers extraordinary powers needing robust independent oversight by the Supreme Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Regarding FICA, the WP did not vote in favour of FICA as promulgated by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We understand that there are foreign actors who wish Singapore harm and that the Government should have powers to combat and counter malignant forces, but our view is that FICA confers extraordinary powers which need the most robust of independent oversight by the judicial arm of our Government, namely, the Supreme Court.

sections.label: WP opposition to POFMA
sections.summary: The WP opposed POFMA because it entrusts Ministers and their alternate authorities to decide what is truth and what is a falsehood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for POFMA, the WP opposed it because POFMA entrusts the Ministers and their alternate authorities to decide what is truth and what is a falsehood.

sections.label: Blocking Asia Sentinel's website
sections.summary: Because Asia Sentinel did not comply fully with the Government's order, Internet service providers in Singapore are ordered to block access to its website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Because Asia Sentinel did not comply fully with the Government's order, Internet service providers in Singapore are ordered to block access in Singapore to Asia Sentinel's website.

sections.label: Correction Notice at article top
sections.summary: A Correction Notice at the top of the article should be sufficient if the Government's concern is Singaporeans reading the Government's point of view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Surely, a Correction Notice situated at the top of the article should be sufficient if the Government's concern is for Singaporeans to be able to read the Government's point of view in contrast to that of the news publication.

sections.label: Asia Sentinel Singapore IP block
sections.summary: Anyone using a Singapore IP address can no longer access any Asia Sentinel articles, even those unrelated to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, anyone using a computer with a Singapore IP address can no longer access any articles published on Asia Sentinel, even those that have nothing to do with Singapore.

sections.label: Resident's scam loss
sections.summary: A resident at the speaker's Meet-the-People Session on Monday said she lost more than $300,000 in total.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The resident at my Meet-the-People Session on Monday told me that she lost more than $300,000 in total.

sections.label: Bill as anti-scam defence
sections.summary: The Bill is hoped to be an important line of defence against online scams, while AI portends more intelligent scammers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While it is hoped that this Bill will serve as an important line of defence to disrupt online scams, the future is even more ominous, with artificial intelligence (AI) portending the prospect of a far more intelligent scammer than ever before.

sections.label: Bill's scope beyond scams
sections.summary: The Bill targets scams and criminal activity, but its explanatory statement says it also seeks to protect against online harms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, the target of the Bill appears to be scams and other criminal activity, but the fact that the explanatory statement says that the Bill seeks to also protect against online harms suggests that activities other than criminal ones have been contemplated by the drafters of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Minister shed light on what other activities the Bill could potentially address or conceivably address?

sections.label: WP support and enforcement powers
sections.summary: The WP will continue to favour the Bill if it stays focused on its target, and it will give enforcement officers proactive powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: POFMA and FICA carry the possibility of Ministers depriving Singaporeans of hearing valid alternative viewpoints without adequate judicial checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If it remains focused on this target, the WP will continue to be in favour of its implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill, if passed, will provide the legislative levers that will enable our enforcement officers to take proactive measures to protect Singapore residents from falling victim to scams.

sections.label: Code of practice legislative effect
sections.summary: Clause 19(4) gives a code of practice effect despite confidentiality duties, while clause 21(4) says it has no legislative effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Clause 19(4) also provides that the requirement of a code of practice has an effect despite any duty of confidentiality, privacy or arising from contract or any rule of professional conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, may I please ask why it is then stipulated in clause 21(4) of the Bill that the code of practice issued under the said clause does not have legislative effect?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Would it not be better to provide that the code of Practice constitutes subsidiary legislation under the Act once it comes into force?

sections.label: Appeals to Minister and Tribunal
sections.summary: Appeals on competent authority decisions go to the Minister, while Government directive and Order appeals go to the Reviewing Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Appeals may be made to the Minister in relation to decisions made by the competent authority under Part 4 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Appeals against actions in relation to Government directives under Part 2 of the Bill and Orders under Part 6 of the Bill may be appealed to the Reviewing Tribunal.

sections.label: Extradition threshold for offences
sections.summary: A two-year maximum makes an offence extraditable if listed as serious, but clause 52's one-year maximum falls below the Extradition Act threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As the said clause provides for a maximum punishment of two years, which is the minimum threshold as provided for in the Extradition Act 1968 for an offence to be an extradition offence, under the current legislative scheme, so long as the Second Schedule of the Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act is subsequently updated to include this specific offence as a “serious offence”, this offence becomes extraditable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is not the case for clause 52 of the Bill which creates the offence for breaching a Part 6 Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is because the maximum punishment for a breach of clause 52 is one year, which is below the minimum threshold provided for in the Extradition Act.

sections.label: Scam losses in 2022
sections.summary: SPF data shows about 31,700 scam victims lost almost $661 million in 2022, $29 million more than the year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to data from SPF, the victims of some 31,700 scam cases were cheated of almost $661 million in 2022, $29 million more than the year before.

sections.label: Blocking suspected scam websites
sections.summary: In 2021, 12,000 suspected scam websites were blocked, many using AI algorithms that detect and block them quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2021, 12,000 suspected scam websites were blocked, many with the help of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms that can quickly detect and block scam websites.

sections.label: ScamShield downloads and telco blocking
sections.summary: The NCPC says over 600,000 people downloaded ScamShield, and the Government should direct telcos to block verified scam messages and calls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The NCPC says that more than 600,000 people have downloaded the ScamShield app.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To better protect potential victims of scams who are unaware of ScamShield or choose not to install the app on their phones, the Government should direct telcos to block all verified scam messages and calls, without depending on end users to install ScamShield.

sections.label: Tackling the scam epidemic
sections.summary: The scam epidemic needs more effective action by the Government, telcos and financial institutions, and the Bill aims to give them more levers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The scam epidemic is a gargantuan problem which needs to be tackled more effectively by the Government, telcos and financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope that this Bill will give these agencies and organisations more levers to do so, to prevent more Singaporeans from falling victim and losing their hard-earned savings to these criminals.

sections.label: CASE e-commerce complaints
sections.summary: CASE received 2,530 e-commerce complaints in 2022 and 1,408 in the first five months of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In 2022, CASE received 2,530 consumer complaints regarding e-commerce purchases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In the first five months of this year alone, CASE has received 1,408 related complaints and this is over 55% of last year's case load.

sections.label: Scammer's Carousell verified tick
sections.summary: A Straits Times article reported that scammer Nicholas Ong Chang Hui obtained a verified tick on Carousell after previously scamming victims there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Over the weekend, Members may have read a The Straits Times article about how Nicholas Ong Chang Hui, a recalcitrant scammer who was sentenced to 23 months and six weeks' imprisonment, was able to obtain a verified tick on Carousell, even after he was caught previously scamming victims on the same platform.

sections.label: Shopee CASE dispute framework
sections.summary: In April this year, Shopee Singapore signed an MOU with CASE to adopt CASE's Standard Dispute Management Framework for E-marketplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In April this year, Shopee Singapore signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with CASE, to adopt CASE's Standard Dispute Management Framework for E-marketplaces.

sections.label: Couple's life savings lost
sections.summary: At a Meet-the-People session, the speaker met a couple who lost over $240,000 in unauthorised bank account transfers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: During my Meet-the-People session this past Monday, I met a couple who had lost their life savings, over $240,000, through elaborate and unauthorised transfers from their bank accounts.

sections.label: Bill measures against online crime
sections.summary: The Bill introduces measures including Government Directions, codes of practice for online service providers, and enhanced Police enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a number of new measures to combat online crime, including: firstly, issuance of Government Directions to online service providers to take down content or disable accounts that are suspected of being used for criminal activity; secondly, online service providers will be required to comply with codes of practice that set out standards for preventing and responding to online harms; thirdly, enhanced enforcement powers allow the Police to investigate and prosecute online crimes.

sections.label: Expedited tribunal appeal rules
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry will consider rules letting the Reviewing Tribunal hear cases on an expedited basis, stay Directions or Orders, or make interim measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the premises, will the Ministry consider establishing rules, possibly by way of a subsidiary legislation, to enabling the Reviewing Tribunal or such other appeals committee, in the appropriate circumstances, to either, first, hear cases on an expedited basis; second, stay the Direction or Order pending the final decision of the Reviewing Tribunal; or third, make interim measures/orders where appropriate and necessary?

sections.label: Periodic review of online harms law
sections.summary: The speaker suggests constant monitoring and review of online criminal harms, and asks the Minister to assure periodic review of the Bill or its Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would humbly suggest a constant monitoring and review of the online criminal harms space in this regard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope that the Minister can assure this House that the Bill or its Schedule can be periodically reviewed on a frequent basis to ensure that we keep up-to-date and possibly even abreast with the various new online criminal harms and technological platforms that may arise in the future so as to ensure that the legislation will still remain fit for purpose.

sections.label: Prevention and public awareness
sections.summary: The speaker urges continuing a proactive approach to preventing online criminal harms by working with stakeholders to raise public awareness and collective vigilance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: At the same time, we should continue with our proactive approach to the prevention of online criminal harms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope that the Ministry will continue the good work by working with all stakeholders, from corporates, online platforms to educational institutions and our youths who are digital natives, in raising public awareness and collective vigilance as a nation against online criminal harms.

sections.label: User vigilance and Online Criminal Harms Bill
sections.summary: The speaker says users must be vigilant and do digital housekeeping, and welcomes the Government enacting the Online Criminal Harms Bill against criminal online content.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As users, we do need to be vigilant against bad actors by setting up our digital house in order and doing the regular "digital spring cleaning" and "digital health checks".

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But given the pervasive threat and grave impact of online criminal harms on victims, it is timely that the Government is enacting this Online Criminal Harms Bill to tackle online content which is criminal in nature or used to facilitate or abet crimes.

sections.label: Government Directions and lower threshold
sections.summary: The speaker states that when enacted, Government Directions may be issued on reasonable suspicion of online criminal activity, with a lower threshold enabling disruption of scams and malicious cyber activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When this Bill is enacted into law, Government Directions may be issued when there is reasonable suspicion that an online activity is being carried out to commit a crime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To ensure speed of response, lower threshold for taking action enables the Government to disrupt scams and malicious cyber activities before anyone falls prey.

sections.label: Balancing enforcement with privacy safeguards
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify how the Government will balance effective law enforcement with privacy rights and legal safeguards in implementing the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can Minister clarify how, in the implementation of this Bill, the Government will balance the need for effective law enforcement with privacy rights and legal safeguards?

sections.label: Live birds sold in Facebook groups
sections.summary: The speaker cites a 2021 Traffic NGO report finding 3,354 live birds on sale in 44 Singapore-based Facebook groups from December 2018 to April 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2021, a report by Traffic, a non-governmental organisation (NGO), found that 3,354 live birds were put on sale in 44 Singapore-based Facebook groups from December 2018 to April 2019.

sections.label: Wildlife trafficking listings and excluded offences
sections.summary: A 2021 report says tech companies blocked nearly 12 million endangered species listings, and asks why certain Act offences are not in the Second Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A 2021 report by the Coalition to End Wildlife Trafficking states that tech companies in the group, including Google, Facebook and TikTok, had blocked or removed nearly 12 million listings of endangered species and associated products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister share why offences under the Animals and Birds Act, Wildlife Act and the Endangered Species (Import and Export) Act have not been included in the Second Schedule?

sections.label: Overseas service providers and individuals
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to elaborate how the rules and offences will operate in practice when service providers or individuals are located overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister elaborate on how these rules and offences will operate in practice when the service providers or individuals are located overseas?

sections.label: Bill's extraterritorial jurisdiction
sections.summary: The Bill is one of the few laws that will have extraterritorial jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, the Bill is one of the few laws that will have extraterritorial jurisdiction.

sections.label: Arrestable and non-bailable offences
sections.summary: Clause 55 makes offences under clauses 50, 51 and 52 arrestable and non-bailable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 55 of the Bill makes offences under clauses 50, 51 and 52 arrestable and non-bailable.

sections.label: Arrestable and non-bailable online harassment concerns
sections.summary: A person suspected of online harassment given a Direction to stop communication who fails to comply faces an arrestable and non-bailable offence, likely remand if charged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the current Bill, if a person was reasonably suspected of, say, online harassment, and was given a Direction to stop communication and fails to comply – the putative offence would have the nature of being arrestable and non-bailable – which means that, if charged, the accused person would likely be held in remand until the matter is concluded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask specifically about this because for most of the offences in Part 1 of the First Schedule, the online harm is sufficiently heinous for a failure to comply with a Part 2 Direction to be considered a serious crime, whereas for some offences, like those in Part 2 of the Protection from Harassment Act, it may not necessarily be so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is also important to note that a similar offence like cyberbullying would also not be an arrestable and non-bailable offence.

sections.label: Bill complements existing legislation
sections.summary: The Bill serves as a valuable complement to existing legislation such as POFMA, FICA and the Broadcasting Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Today, we must remain vigilant and employ more sophisticated means to identify and combat these illicit activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill serves as a valuable complement to our existing legislation, such as POFMA, FICA and the Broadcasting Act.

sections.label: Offences outside Singapore
sections.summary: Clause 56 of the Bill allows individuals committing offences outside Singapore to be dealt with as if committed wholly within Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 56 of the Bill indicates that individuals committing offences outside Singapore may be dealt with as if the offences were committed wholly within Singapore.

sections.label: Falsehoods and foreign interference
sections.summary: The passage asks how the law impacts falsehoods or foreign interference by state actors and whether it overlaps with FICA or POFMA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How does this law also impact on falsehoods or foreign interference by state actors that may seek to destabilise our society?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will this law also have overlaps with FICA or POFMA?

sections.label: Public online safety education
sections.summary: The passage states that educating the public on online safety, scams and responsible digital practices should be prioritised through programmes and campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is essential to prioritise efforts to educate the public about online safety, raise awareness about common scams and promote responsible digital practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This can be achieved through robust digital literacy programmes, continuous education initiatives and comprehensive awareness campaigns, especially for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By strengthening these initiatives, we can equip individuals with the necessary knowledge and skills to navigate the digital landscape safely and confidently.

sections.label: Clause 6 thresholds and preparation
sections.summary: The passage states clause 6(1)(a) describes the general threshold and clause 6(1)(b) the threshold for scams and malicious cyber activities, covering preparation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I may not have specifically used clause 6(1)(a), which describes the general threshold, and clause 6(1)(b) which describes the threshold for scams and malicious cyber activities.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But it is this – clause 6(1)(b) also covers the preparation for the offence, even when the offence has not yet occurred.

sections.label: No breaking end-to-end encryption
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill will not require online companies to break end-to-end encryption in private messaging.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, this Bill will not require online companies to “break” end-to-end encryption in private messaging.

sections.label: Scope to existing offences
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill applies only to online content and activity that already constitute a criminal offence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Bill, as it stands, applies only to online content and activity that already constitute a criminal offence in Singapore, such as incitement to hatred against a religious group.

sections.label: Directions to entities without presence
sections.summary: The Bill allows Directions, Notices, Directives and Orders to be issued to entities and individuals with no presence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Bill has provisions that allow us to issue Directions, Notices, Directives and Orders to entities and individuals, even if they have no presence in Singapore.

sections.label: Access Blocking Order example
sections.summary: An Access Blocking Order can be issued to Internet access service providers to stop non-compliant online services reaching users in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, an Access Blocking Order can be issued to Internet access service providers to prevent non-compliant online services from continuing to reach users in Singapore and do them harm.

sections.label: Penalties aligned with FICA POFMA
sections.summary: The penalties in the Online Criminal Harms Act are aligned with similar legislation such as FICA and POFMA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The penalties in the Online Criminal Harms Act are aligned with similar legislation, such as FICA and POFMA.

sections.label: Broader scope of online harms
sections.summary: The Online Criminal Harms Bill will cover a broader scope of online criminal harms, including illegal moneylending, unlawful gambling and drug-related offences.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Online Criminal Harms Bill will cover a broader scope of online criminal harms, including illegal moneylending, unlawful gambling and drug-related offences.

sections.label: Directions against scams and cyber activities
sections.summary: The Online Criminal Harms Act will provide the Government targeted levers to issue Directions against scams and malicious cyber activities, including suspected preparation for such offences.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: A user submits a report, the code says, you, as a social media service, have a responsibility to act on that report.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But given the need to protect victims from falling prey to scams and to ensure that scams can be efficiently and effectively addressed, the Online Criminal Harms Act, when it takes effect, will take one step further to provide the Government with the targeted levers to issue Directions against scams and malicious cyber activities, including against online activity that is suspected to be in preparation for such offences.

sections.label: Competent authority within Singapore Police Force
sections.summary: The competent authority will be sited within the Singapore Police Force and structurally separate from Police units performing investigative functions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The competent authority will be sited within the Singapore Police Force (SPF), and will be structurally separate from the Police units that perform investigative functions.

sections.label: Codes of practice purposes
sections.summary: The codes of practice provide user verification and payment protections and apply to designated online services, including e-commerce platforms posing significant scam risk.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The purposes of the codes of practice are set out in the Third Schedule, and they do provide for user verification and payment protections.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Codes will apply to designated online services, which can include e-commerce platforms that are assessed to pose significant risk of scams or malicious cyber activities.

sections.label: Stay would cause harm
sections.summary: A stay on reconsideration or appeal would mean more people continue to be harmed by online criminal activity.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The answer is yes, because any stay on reconsideration or appeal would mean that more people would continue to be harmed by the online criminal activity.

sections.label: Bill's current offence focus
sections.summary: The Bill currently focuses on criminal offences pertaining to national security, national harmony and individual safety.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For now, the Bill focuses on criminal offences that pertain to national security, national harmony and individual safety.

sections.label: Analytics and AI use
sections.summary: The Government is making more use of analytics and AI, for example to detect and shut down scam websites faster.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government is making more use of analytics and also AI, for example, to detect and shut down scam websites faster.

sections.label: Protections and circumvention risk
sections.summary: The Government will protect people in Singapore from online criminal content, but individuals who circumvent protections via VPN do so at their own risk.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government will do its best to protect the people in Singapore by preventing online criminal content and activities from reaching them.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, if individuals choose to circumvent these protections and use VPN or other means to access dubious content sources, they do so at their own risk.

sections.label: Anti-scam outreach initiatives
sections.summary: Initiatives include disseminating scam advisories, sharing successful prosecutions, an e-shoppers watch group, and collaborations with platforms and retailers on anti-scam messages.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Some of these initiatives include proactive dissemination of information and advisories on scams and sharing of successful prosecutions on a regular basis; e-shoppers on watch interest group, collaborations with e-commerce platforms such as Shopee for the interactive in-app anti-scam quiz and collaborations with retailers such as Gardenia, iJooz and Canadian Pizza to display anti-scam messages on their platforms.

sections.label: Blocking scam calls, international call option
sections.summary: IMDA is considering letting phone users block all international calls, and over 55 million calls are blocked daily.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If my memory serves me right, as recently as February or March, I think we updated the House that upwards of 55 million calls are blocked every single day right now.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Calls are not the primary target of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Calls are an important way in which scammers reach their victims and we have taken active steps to block them.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I can update the House that IMDA is seriously looking at giving phone users the option to block all international calls, which is primarily how scam calls get piped through.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: That is something in the works, and I hope to be able to give Members an update in the not-too-distant future.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will continue to improve the product to make it more robust and make it easier, as you say, for people to report the scams and to as best as possible, try and block the verified scam callers, as well as content.

sections.label: SMS not online scam
sections.summary: SMS is not offered online, so SMSes are not strictly covered by the online scam definition.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Technically speaking, SMS is not anything that is offered online.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If we apply the strict definition of an online scam, SMSes are not strictly covered.

sections.label: Account verification as intervention
sections.summary: Account verification is a potential useful area of intervention, though no decision has been made.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I do not want to give the impression that this is what has been decided.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But one of the potential and, I think, a very useful area of intervention has to do with account verification.

sections.label: Confirming goods before money release
sections.summary: Another possibly useful intervention is requiring confirmation that the good was received before money is released.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The other probably useful intervention is in terms of requiring some confirmation that the good has been received before the money is released.
